boundaries: Effects are often observed in preclinical models or specific patient subgroups; generalizability across all solid tumors is limited by individual variability and tumor microenvironment differences.
contribution: Details how specific metabolites (SCFAs, tryptophan derivatives, bile acids) influence ICI efficacy by modulating the PD-1/PD-L1 axis. For example, butyrate enhances CD8+ T-cell function and stemness, while kynurenine promotes exhaustion. It also notes that some metabolites (e.g., high-dose propionate) can upregulate PD-L1, indicating complex dose/tumor-type dependent effects.
possible_uses: Use to explain the bidirectional and context-dependent nature of microbiome modulation of ICI efficacy. Cite specific examples of metabolites that enhance or inhibit response to illustrate heterogeneity.

boundaries: Many mechanistic insights are derived from mouse models or in vitro studies; direct causal chains in human patients are often inferred from correlative clinical data and require further validation.
contribution: Elaborates on the molecular mechanisms: 1) Epigenetic regulation (Butyrate as HDAC inhibitor affecting Pdcd1 promoter); 2) Receptor-mediated signaling (AhR, FXR, TGR5, GPCRs); 3) Metabolic reprogramming (Propionate promoting OXPHOS in T cells); 4) Modulation of stromal/immune cells (MDSCs, TAMs, DCs).
possible_uses: Use to construct the mechanistic section of the review. Provide specific pathway details (e.g., Butyrate-HDAC-FOXO1, Kynurenine-AhR-PD-L1) to support claims about how the microbiome biologically influences checkpoint blockade.

boundaries: Predictive models are often cancer-specific (e.g., HCC, NSCLC, Melanoma) and require validation in larger, diverse cohorts. Lack of standardized assays limits clinical adoption.
contribution: Reviews clinical evidence for metabolite-based biomarkers (e.g., fecal bile acid profiles, plasma SCFAs) and functional metagenomic signatures (e.g., but gene cluster) predicting ICI response.
possible_uses: Use to discuss the current state of biomarker development for patient stratification. Highlight the shift from taxonomic to functional/metabolic biomarkers.

boundaries: Most interventions are in early-stage trials or preclinical phases. Challenges include standardization, safety, delivery methods, and individual variability in response.
contribution: Summarizes clinical and preclinical data on microbiota-targeted interventions: FMT (restoring responder microbiota), probiotics/prebiotics (modulating metabolite production), and direct metabolite supplementation/engineered bacteria.
possible_uses: Use to discuss therapeutic strategies aimed at overcoming ICI resistance. Illustrate the progression from broad interventions (FMT) to precision approaches (engineered bacteria, defined consortia).
